name: Sheared LLaMA: Accelerating Language Model Pre-training via Structured Pruning
problem: Training a competitive 1-3B model from scratch on trillions of tokens is expensive; is there a cheaper route to a small capable model than pretraining?
mechanism: TARGETED structured pruning to an exact target SHAPE (remove whole layers, attention heads, and intermediate/hidden dimensions end-to-end, keeping the residual architecture valid) rather than unstructured pruning, which keeps a dense-shaped model with no speed benefit. Paired with DYNAMIC BATCH LOADING: reweight the sampling of each training batch toward the domains with the highest current loss, which is what makes recovery from the pruning damage fast on a small compute budget.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): Sheared-LLaMA 1.3B and 2.7B, pruned from LLaMA2-7B, outperform SOTA open models of equivalent size (Pythia, INCITE, OpenLLaMA, TinyLlama) across downstream and instruction-tuning evaluations, WHILE REQUIRING ONLY 3% OF THE COMPUTE compared to training such models from scratch. COMPRESSION RATIO: 7B -> 1.3B or 2.7B is 2.6x or 5.4x fewer parameters, all of it structural so the speedup is real. QUALITY COST: no perplexity delta in the abstract; the reported axis is 'beats same-size models from scratch at 3% of the compute'. Note this is a TRAINING-cost claim about producing a small model, not an inference-compression claim about serving a large one.
